chapter_theme: The way of one who does not do virtue (அறஞ்செயான் திறம்): the hoarder's wealth is poison fruit, the unvirtuous see bodies perish and still learn nothing, disease and hell await them; joy and sorrow come from past deeds, so give and praise the Lord instead of flattering the rich.
structure_note: Wasted wealth and wasted days (260, 261); what the unvirtuous lack and suffer (262 to 266); joy and sorrow as the fruit of deeds, and the call to give and worship (267 to 269).

260.reading: The wealth of those who do no clinging good is like the large fruit of the poisonous etti that ripens and falls; base wretches who heap it up by lending at interest and scoop it into the ground do not know what it is for.
260.nuance: எட்டி is the strychnine tree, whose fruit looks ripe but cannot be eaten. ஒட்டிய நல்லறம் is taken as virtue that stays with one beyond death. Usury (வட்டி) is singled out as the way such wealth is gathered.

261.reading: The ages have gone, aeons have passed, plans have run out and the days grow short; even seeing bodies, sources of great affliction, destroyed as if wrung out, they do not know virtue.
261.nuance: கற்பனை may be imaginings and plans, or kalpa, the aeon, echoing ஊழி in line 1. பிழிந்தன போல (as if squeezed) gives the body as something wrung dry.

262.reading: Those who do not know virtue do not know how to think of the Lord's feet and do not know even the outskirts of Siva's city; many of them, listening to false words, know only wrongdoing and stay fixed in enmity.
262.nuance: மறம் here is the opposite of அறம், wrongdoing, not the martial valour it means in war poetry. The chain runs from not knowing virtue to not knowing the Lord: ethics comes first.

263.reading: Cough, wasting, phlegm and fever belong to those who do not do good; thunderbolt, snake, rohini and tumour do not come near those who do.
263.nuance: The verse makes virtue a literal protection against illness and mishap. உரோணி is unclear: a disease of the throat in some lists, or the star Rohini as an evil influence.

264.reading: You do not praise the Supreme who is to be praised, do not give even a little to those who beg, do not water and raise groves with a pot; will you stand in hell, good-hearted ones?
264.nuance: The groves (கா) are taken as flower gardens kept for worship. நல்நெஞ்சினீரே may be ironic or a sincere appeal to people capable of better. ஈதலை யாயினும் is unclear; read as 'even a little'.

265.reading: Those who stray from the path go back into the womb, while those who keep to it, driving off the stain of deeds, stand high; without walking the path no one reaches the world of the gods.
265.nuance: The verse plays on வழி (path) and கழி (going astray). கருப்பு ஆரும் is read as entering the womb again; மழிநடக்கும் is obscure and the reading of lines 1 to 3 is a guess at the plain contrast.

266.reading: Those who have ripened see the Lord's feet, the resolute rule his heaven, but the swollen-headed die without a single support, fallen into a withering anger.
266.nuance: கனிந்தவர் (ripened, softened) is commonly taken as those mellowed in love, துணிந்தவர் as those who boldly renounced, மலிந்தவர் as those swollen with wealth or pride. மெலிந்த சினம் is obscure.

267.reading: Joy and sorrow, the two, are settled by what one did before; fools who see joy and still do not give, loveless in mind, do not know virtue.
267.nuance: The argument is from cause: present joy is the fruit of past good, so withholding now spends it without renewal. Lack of giving is traced to lack of love (அன்பிலார்).

268.reading: The Lord of unfailing renown decides ruin and gain and will not let you seek pleasure by doing what is unfair; think of offering and giving, and if you do what brings joy it will be like a cow that yields.
268.nuance: இடுவதும் ஈவதும் may be offering (to God or fire) and giving (to people). பசுவது வாமே is obscure: a cow that keeps giving milk, or பசு in the Siddhanta sense of the bound soul.

269.reading: Do not wither praising petty-minded men for their wealth in hope of a living; with your true home in mind, praise the Lord, as an archer fixes his mark to hit the target.
269.nuance: இல்லம் கருதி may mean thinking of one's household or of the final home with the Lord. Line 1 (சிலர்பலர் வாழ்வெனும்) is compressed. The archer image asks for a single aim.

links.note: Both compare unshared wealth to the fruit of the poisonous etti. In the Kural it ripens in the middle of town where no one can use it; in Tirumular it ripens and falls, and the usurer buries his store in the ground.
Both fault the person who watches beauty, youth and bodies pass and still does no good thing.
The Kural says the fiery disease of hunger will not touch one who shares his food; Tirumular extends the promise to cough, fever and tumour, taking literally what the Kural keeps to hunger.
Both read present fortune as the fruit of past virtue: the Kural points to the palanquin's bearer and rider, Tirumular to joy and sorrow settled by former deeds.
Both refuse gain got by leaving fairness: the Kural says to give it up the same day, Tirumular that the Lord will not let pleasure sought that way stand.

source_issues: 260: line 3 reads கொணடு, a misprint for கொண்டு.
265: மழிநடக்கும் in line 3 is obscure and may be corrupt.
